_readme: Accepted-measurement policies for AnonRouter's own confidential gateway (the
first of the two hops this SDK verifies). The second hop, the upstream model
provider's enclave, is pinned separately in measurements.json.
THIS FILE MUST NEVER BE FETCHED FROM THE GATEWAY IT DESCRIBES. A verifier that
downloads its allowlist from the server it is verifying can always be handed an
allowlist naming that server. It ships inside the published packages instead, and
the CI parity gate proves the JavaScript and Python copies never drift.
status=published  a released plane, resolved by verifyGateway() by default.
status=candidate  a reviewed but pre-release plane whose pins are expected to
move. Requires allowCandidate: true, so a default call can
never quietly pass against a plane that is not released.
Every switch in a policy is REQUIRED. A truncated or hand-edited policy fails to
parse rather than silently disabling a check.

policies.notes: AnonRouter confidential content plane running in an Intel TDX CVM. Published from the independently retained production release manifest with SHA-256 ebb976a12b274afc34fb31459578e3ef107764d697ef074d1a82b27d79b1707c. That manifest binds reviewed source commit e792667508edc4e2c06b5f058cccd7b3e077b0a8, the exact measured app compose, digest-pinned content-plane image, app id, instance id, canonical production origin, TLS SPKI and platform measurements. api.private.anonrouter.ai is retained as an attested alias; api.anonrouter.ai is the customer default. The release id is not treated as sufficient identity: app id, compose hash and every platform measurement remain independently pinned. Three third-party source-to-digest provenance gaps named in the manifest remain supply-chain limitations, not attestation bypasses. requireHardwareVerified remains true, so verification fails closed unless a DCAP chain verifier is supplied.
